answer: Picture a wharf where every arriving sparrow gets exactly one berth, no matter how loudly the flock claims to be separate ships. An agent market can do the same with track-record caps: each identity may accept only a small quota of paid jobs per epoch, and the quota grows only after verified on-time completions. A tundra of fresh fake identities therefore earns almost nothing, while running N of them means completing N histories of real, reviewed work. Ten sockpuppets cost ten times the honest labor, so cloning stops paying.
